text.p: - April monthly inflation rose to two percent from 0.3 percent in March, while year-on-year inflation rose to 8.2 percent compared to 7.4 in the previous year, the Slovenian Statistical Office reported.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said this year's inflation will be lower than 8.8 percent in 1996.
- Drnovsek said he would meet parliamentary parties to seek support for a constitutional amendment to enable foreigners to own real estate in Slovenia.
- Slovenian railway workers, demanding higher wages, will continue negotiations with management on May 5. If talks again prove unsuccessful, a third strike will be staged on May 6.
- President Milan Kucan visited his Hungarian counterpart Arpad Goncz. They discussed mutual relations, efforts of both countries to join NATO and the EU and minorities' rights in both states.
- Two bears from Slovenian forests will be sent to France in an effort to prevent bears dying out in that region.
- Shareholders of listed warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC on Tuesday approved the company's plan to seek fresh capital in order to finance new investment.
